storm.summary_layperson: Thunderstorms embedded in a band of showers are moving through the area right now, with radar showing cells within a few miles of the cove and a Flood Watch in effect until 2 AM for heavy rain and possible flash flooding.
storm.local_effect_blurb: The Sound isn't offering any buffer tonight — the air-water gap is already down to about -2°F (air cooler than water), below the ~5°F threshold needed for a protective marine layer, so the cove sees the same storm activity as inland towns.
storm.detail_html:
An upper-level disturbance and a stalled boundary are interacting with the afternoon sea breeze and a moisture-rich air mass to produce embedded thunderstorms and heavy rainfall across the area, per the NWS Upton forecast discussion. A Flood Watch is in effect for the region until 2 AM, driven mainly by rainfall totals of three-quarters to one inch, not by wind or hail.

Radar out of KOKX shows a cluster of cells 1.2 to 5.1 miles WSW through NW of the cove, each in the 35–39 dBZ range and closing at 11–20 kt. The nearest cell's projected arrival time has already passed as of the most recent scan — storms are likely over or immediately adjacent to the cove right now, so this is a live situation, not a forecast.

Neither of the cove's usual local defenses is working tonight. The marine layer (the cool-water buffer that can weaken incoming storms) is absent — water and air temperatures are within about 2°F of each other, well short of the ~5°F gap the mechanism needs. The sea breeze is also inactive, so there's no directional shielding either. The cove is exposed the same as Stamford, Rye, or any other shoreline town tonight.

Instability is modest (CAPE only 190 J/kg) but deep-layer shear is strong (57 kt from the WSW), which favors organized, longer-lived convection over isolated pulse storms. The AFD expects the showers-and-thunderstorm activity to continue from late afternoon into the evening.

What would push this to high: a Severe Thunderstorm or Flash Flood Warning being issued, or a cell within 25 miles reaching 45+ dBZ on a track toward the cove. Neither condition is currently met, but given the overdue cell, re-check radar before making any on-water decisions.

wind.tactics_blurb: Light, wandering gradient wind (5–7 kt, N to NNE) with no sea-breeze component tonight, but several thunderstorm cells are within a few miles of the cove right now, so any breeze could turn into a sudden gusty outflow with little warning. Not a night to commit to a favored side — stay flexible and watch the sky more than the wind gauge.
wind.tactics_detail_html:
Tonight is a gradient-only day (no sea breeze): the land-water temperature difference (deltaT) is actually negative, about -2°F — the inland air is slightly cooler than the Sound — and the sea-breeze station network shows it building on only 33% of coastal stations, well short of what an active thermal needs. With the sea-breeze ingredient absent, this is classified as a light gradient-wind day (internally "B-light"): mean authoritative wind speed across the well-sited stations is just 5.1 kt.

Direction is unsettled. The station ensemble median points ESE (122°) but Riverside YC itself is reading NE (47°) at only 2.1 kt, and agreement across the whole station network is just 38%. That spread isn't the cove sheltering from a cleaner open-Sound flow — it's the regional wind itself being disorganized because of the thunderstorms moving through the area, not cove geography.

Model wind guidance (HRRR) is only usable through 19:00 EDT tonight — three hours into this five-hour window. The 20:00–22:00 rows above are a persistence-based estimate, not a model forecast, and should be read as directional guidance only.

The overriding factor tonight is convective, not synoptic: radar shows several storm cells 1–5 miles from the cove, with the nearest one already overdue for arrival as of the last scan — it may be over the course right now. Any cell passing near or over the racecourse can throw a 20–30 kt outflow gust regardless of the ambient gradient wind, which would swamp anything in the table above.

Practical call: no side of the course is reliably favored in light, disorganized flow like this, and with an active Flood Watch and thunderstorms in the immediate area, tonight is a night to prioritize getting boats off the water over racing tactics.
